Their customers will need data connectivity from vPLC environments to historians, MES, and cloud — and Tracebook-style AI support as the install base grows.

When plants adopt vPLC, the connectivity question shifts: how does data get from the soft controller to analytics and MES? DIME handles that path. And as OTee's install base grows, engineers will ask the same 10 questions about configuration over and over — exactly the use case Tracebook was built for. He's cross-functional at OTee (customer success, product, sales engineering) so he's the right person to have the conversation with.

Transporting data is a solved problem, but ensuring an AI model can contextualise, trust, and verify the lineage of a legacy edge sensor input is where the real friction lies. Bridging that data gap down to the legacy edge is where we have focused.' This maps directly to what DIME and i3X do for manufacturing.
